Lemma 2 B1/B2 correct: x==const contradicts dominance; z==z0 const with x nonconst gives e^{x(s)}=R(x(s))=-x(s)^2+c and, differentiating and cancelling x' (not identically 0), e^{x(s)}=R'(x(s))=-2x(s), so x(s) lies in roots of fixed nonzero quadratic X^2-2X-c (leading coeff -1), hence constant — contradiction. Uses only that z0 not in Lambda (automatic as E bounded). Lemma 3 correct modulo explicitly cited black box: M=C(x(s),z(s)) has trdeg<=1; e^x in M(wp(z)); wp'(z) algebraic over M(wp(z)) via (wp')^2=4wp^3-8, so trdeg(L/C)<=2. Translation X=x-x(s0), Z=z-z(s0) preserves trdeg (e^X=e^{-x(s0)}e^x; wp(z) in C0(wp(Z),wp'(Z)) by Weierstrass addition formula for z0 not in Lambda). Degree<=4 never used, so exclusion holds at every degree — stronger than required, still satisfies fallback. Lemma 1(f) smooth-point/nonemptiness argument has a boundary nuance (if the lift z0 of 2 lies on partial(F0), the wp-image of a half-neighbourhood is not open; basis of Lambda not fixed), but (f) is inessential to the exclusion and is listed as limitation, not a failure of the success criterion. No computation error, no boundary condition missed in the essential chain.
